notes: id = value to pass in the OpenAI-compatible "model" request field (llama.cpp router) or as --model to query_lm.py/agent_lm.py (LM Studio, using the LM Studio model id noted in backends.lm_studio.notes when different from this id). source_dir is the real (two-level) path under the scanned cache; router-mode --models-dir scans only one level, so a flat symlink farm named <org>__<repo> is generated at router_models_dir and used as the actual --models-dir target. model_file is what gets passed to --model (first shard only for multipart). mmproj_file is auto-paired by llama-server via --mmproj when present, not a separate model. backends.<name>.status is one of: working (empirically confirmed via a real load+inference test), rejected (empirically confirmed to fail, e.g. a memory guardrail), untested (no real test run yet -- absence of a rejection is NOT evidence it works), not_configured (backend has no launcher/setup on this machine yet). backends.<name> perf fields (populated only when status=working, from a single small chat-completion test, not a statistical average -- treat as one data point, not a benchmark): load_time_s = time to load weights + get the child server listening, isolated from inference time (from the server's own 'model loaded' log timestamp where available, else total_elapsed_s minus inference time); total_elapsed_s = full curl round-trip (load + prompt processing + generation); prompt_tokens_per_second / gen_tokens_per_second = from the response's own "timings" object.
